root.name: Ware Opening: Cologne Gambit
root.moves: 1. a4 b6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Nd7

overview: A Ware Opening line where after 1.a4 b6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nd7 White typically plays 4.e4, offering a pawn for development. Black has a solid set-up with the knight on d7 and can take on e4. I am unsure of the theory; this is an obscure irregular line.

white_ideas.idea: Play e4 to open the centre with a lead in development
Use the Nc3 and Bf4 for central play

black_ideas.idea: Take on e4 and hold the pawn
Develop the bishop to b7 and use the long diagonal

typical_structures.structure: Black queenside fianchetto with d5 and Nd7; White a-pawn pushed

character.notes: A pawn offer in an irregular line leads to unbalanced play.

gambit.notes: The e4 pawn can be taken and kept.

soundness.notes: White's a4 and pawn offer are thought to give too little.

structure.notes: Open centre after exchanges on e4.

approach.notes: 1.a4 and this gambit are very rare among strong players.

level.notes: Obscure and dubious, not a good repertoire base.
